cumleler: Why are pure tones avoided in loudspeaker hearing tests?
A pure tone from a loudspeaker reflects off the room's walls.
Reflections overlap the direct sound; this creates standing waves.
The level can change markedly with a move of a few centimeters.
So warble tones or narrowband noise are used instead.
Their energy spreads over a small frequency range, keeping levels stable.
